doc.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Ross first sees Tommy's arrangements with Dean Hudson
summary: With Dean Hudson at 16 or 17, Ross found good arrangements by Tommy via trumpeter Johnny Presley.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah, I guess now you either go in the service or you go to college. When we were young you’d go out on the road with some band. That’s the first time I saw Tommy Newsom arrangements. I was playing with a territory band down south. I was 16 or 17 years old. Dean Hudson. It was a famous band in its neighborhood. And your friend Johnny Presley was one of the trumpet players, from Virginia. And I’d say, “This is better arrangements than we usually have, where’d you get these?” And he said, “Well my friend, Tommy Newsom.” I didn’t even know him then.
I didn’t know Johnny had that music.
Can you send him a bill or is it too late?
Well he was going to sing so it was like vocal arrangements but there would be an ensemble in the middle. It was better than Hudson’s usual stuff.
